dedupe_keys.name: mapyourgrid open initiative to map the world s electricity transmission grids in openstreetmap

description: MapYourGrid is a free, open-source initiative that trains and supports volunteers, communities and organisations to map electricity grids in OpenStreetMap, which it describes as the de facto standard for global grid data. Its stated aims are an open digital twin of the European grid and raising global transmission grid coverage in OpenStreetMap from 75% to 98% by 2028, especially in developing countries where gaps limit energy access and clean energy planning. Coverage: global, with a progress page counting mapped power towers, power lines and contributors using the project hashtag, and a map of countries where critical grid gaps were closed. Format and access: the mapped data live in OpenStreetMap and can be browsed on Open Infrastructure Map; MapYourGrid provides training, validation strategies, open-source tools, a Discord community and paid services such as model-ready datasets and GIS integration. Licence: the data are OpenStreetMap data, under the Open Database License; the licences of MapYourGrid's own tools were not read. Caveats: coverage and quality vary by country and depend on volunteer effort; the progress figures were not read. Simulation uses: more complete transmission topology for power flow, cascading failure and hazard exposure models. Related records: Open Infrastructure Map (data-open-infrastructure-map) shows the data, PyPSA-Eur's OpenStreetMap network (data-pypsa-eur-osm-prebuilt-network) is built from it, and FLOSM (data-flosm-power-grid-map-and-exports) offers exports.
